name: Sofia Valdez
life: “I still remember trying to learn a driver's breathing from their choice of music.” Thursday often includes a stop at Paper & Pine Books, where Sofia starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I can tell when the driver is scared because the radio gets louder. We agreed on one quiet song.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a washed violet jersey and a narrow brass watch set a little fast. Sofia has a round face with a pronounced chin, with a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow. Sofia presses the lips together to keep a smile in during a conversation.
personality: Sofia finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To agree one quiet song for the hard section.
family: Carmen Kapoor is Sofia’s cousin. Sofia brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Carmen makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *Nine unpaid hours*, Carmen says, “I used to accept cash so nobody asked about my papers.”
connections: Dale Pierce. A familiar song and a cup at the far end provide two markers for a practice drive.

reactions.response: Sofia treats turning back as a completed decision and finds somewhere calm to stop.

reactions.response: Sofia writes down the shift time accurately, then helps them explain the circumstances without having to tell the whole room.

reactions.situation: When somebody waves from across traffic
reactions.response: Sofia waits at the corner to hear their voice and give them a proper answer.
